Carved Briar Tobacco Pipe
Bent Smoking Pipe With Red Swirl Stem
Briar Wood & Acrylic, Approximately 5 Inches
This vintage estate tobacco smoking pipe features a carved briar bowl in a rounded bent apple profile with a rich reddish-brown finish. Fitted with a silver-tone metal shank band and a curved mouthpiece in marbled red acrylic, it exemplifies mid-to-late 20th century pipe craftsmanship. Carved briar pipes are valued by enthusiasts for their tactile grip and heat dissipation.
Hand-carved scroll and channel texture across the rounded briar bowl
Bent ruby red swirl acrylic stem with silver-tone metal accent band
Stamped numbers 048 and 18 on shank near the band
Measures approximately 5 inches in overall length with a 1.9-inch bowl height
Condition:
Previously smoked estate condition. Bowl shows normal carbon cake and rim char from use. Exterior briar carving remains intact with minor surface handling wear. Stem is secure with minor tooth chatter near the lip. Metal collar is firmly seated.

Man Smoking Pipe Folk Art Sculpture

Rendered from solid wood, the piece features expressive facial carving, rhythmic gouge work, and contrasting dark-stained accents that highlight the organic grain and textures of the timber.
